title: When God Seems Silent: 4 Reasons and One Next Step
hook: If God feels silent, don’t panic—start here.
script: You're not broken. David said, "My God, why have You forsaken me?" and heard nothing at first (Psalm 22:1-2). Scripture names four honest reasons. Formation and timing grow endurance (James 1:2-4). Sometimes God already spoke in His Word and in Jesus (Hebrews 1:1-2). He often whispers beneath the noise, not in the wind or fire (1 Kings 19:11-13). And clung-to sin can cloud fellowship (Psalm 66:18). Today try the 4R Plan: repent plainly, return to one chapter, remain in community by texting a believer, and record one small providence. Pray, "Speak, Lord; Your servant is listening," then be still for thirty seconds.

title: The 4R Plan for God’s Silence
hook: If you're tired of waiting on God, listen to this.
script: Waiting feels like a hallway with no doors. But silence can be an invitation. Here's a simple 4R plan for today. Repent: name anything you know is off, ask for clean hands (Psalm 66:18; 1 John 1:9). Return: read Hebrews 1:1-2 or Psalm 27 aloud and look for one phrase. Remain: message a trusted believer and ask, "Will you pray with me this week?" Record: write one line about today's small mercy, even if it's just breath in your lungs. Close with, "Your will, not mine." Journal this question: What did I notice when I slowed down?

title: Hearing the Whisper: 30 Seconds to Recenter
hook: If God feels silent right now, watch this to the end.
script: Elijah looked for God in wind, quake, and fire, but heard Him in a gentle whisper (1 Kings 19:11-13). Sometimes we miss God because life is louder. For the next thirty seconds, pause the scroll. Say, "Speak, Lord." Open Psalm 22:1-2 and let honest words be yours. Then read one verse from the Gospels, because God has spoken by His Son (Hebrews 1:1-2). Ask, "Jesus, what are You highlighting for me today?" Write down the first true, Scripture-shaped thought. Silence doesn't equal absence. It may be invitation. Rewatch this when noise rises, and meet Him again.
